questions.stem: How well do static measures such as CVP and PAOP predict fluid responsiveness?
In a passive leg raise test, a responder is one whose SV or CO changes by ____.
What variability (%) in SVV, PPV, SPV or IVC suggests fluid responsiveness?
What conditions must be met for respiratory variation tests to be valid?
questions.answer: Sinus rhythm, no spontaneous breaths, tidal volume 8 ml/kg

questions.stem: After a 500 ml fluid challenge, what rise in cardiac output defines fluid responsiveness?
What kind of measure is fluid responsiveness?
Where on the Starling curve is a fluid-responsive heart?
In practice, fluid therapy moves a patient from hypovolaemia towards ____.
How many fluid-responsiveness methods have proven good accuracy?
Which clinical signs are used as static tests of fluid responsiveness?
questions.answer: Heart rate, blood pressure, collapsed veins, capillary refill time, recent urine output

questions.stem: Since which year has CVP been used to guide fluid therapy?
A CVP below ____ suggests hypovolaemia.
A CVP above ____ makes a patient unlikely to respond to IV fluid.
How well does PAOP (PCWP) predict fluid responsiveness?
options: It predicts it only when high

questions.stem: A PAOP (PCWP) below ____ suggests hypovolaemia.
Why is IVC ultrasound size a poor predictor of fluid responsiveness?
questions.answer: It tracks CVP, so shares its weakness

questions.stem: How valuable are lactate or SvO2 as tests of fluid responsiveness?
What is the principle of a dynamic test of fluid responsiveness?
questions.answer: Make a brief change in preload and watch the effect on cardiac output

questions.stem: A dynamic fluid challenge is a rapid IV infusion of ____ ml.
Which mini-challenge predicts the response to a 500 ml fluid challenge?
What is the main risk of a dynamic fluid challenge?
In a passive leg raise test, what is the starting position?
In a passive leg raise test, what position is the patient moved into?
questions.answer: Head flat and legs lifted to 45 degrees

questions.stem: The peak effect of a passive leg raise occurs at ____ seconds.
In preload-dependent patients, when does aortic flow peak after a passive leg raise?
Assess the passive leg raise response within ____ of starting it.
What mechanism makes a passive leg raise an autotransfusion?
A passive leg raise shifts about ____ of blood from the calves.
What are the advantages of the passive leg raise test?
questions.answer: Reversible, non-invasive, well validated; works with spontaneous breathing and arrhythmias

questions.stem: What are the disadvantages of the passive leg raise test?
questions.answer: Unreliable in severe hypovolaemia; repositioning may not be possible

questions.stem: An end-expiratory occlusion test holds expiration for ____ seconds.
After an end-expiratory occlusion hold, which change predicts responsiveness accurately?
questions.answer: A rise in pulse pressure or cardiac index

questions.stem: During an end-expiratory occlusion hold, what does the hold act like?
What are the disadvantages of the end-expiratory occlusion hold?
questions.answer: Patient must not breathe spontaneously during the pause; less validated

questions.stem: Name the three respiratory variation indices of pulse and stroke volume.
questions.answer: Systolic pressure variation (SPV), pulse pressure variation (PPV), stroke volume variation (SVV)

questions.stem: What is the formula for pulse pressure variation (PPV)?
Fluid responders have a PPV above ____.
Which PPV range is a grey zone for fluid responsiveness?
Which index is more reliable for fluid responsiveness, PPV or SPV?
What is the formula for stroke volume variation (SVV)?
Fluid responsiveness is shown by an SVV above ____.
Which two devices use a central line, an arterial line and thermodilution to assess fluid responsiveness?
Which device uses an SpO2 probe to assess respiratory variation?
What is the simplest bedside way to judge respiratory variation?
questions.answer: Eyeballing the respiratory swing on the arterial or SpO2 trace

questions.stem: Which breathing pattern limits the accuracy of respiratory variation tests?
What minimum tidal volume does a respiratory variation test need for valid results?
Beyond right- and left-sided measures, which other focused echo tests assess fluid responsiveness?
questions.answer: E/Ea, PLR or EEO combined with echo, IVO, STE

questions.stem: What does focused echocardiography help with in fluid-responsiveness assessment?
Focused echo is an indirect measure of fluid status; what should it be combined with to detect overload?
What sign on focused lung ultrasound indicates fluid overload?
